heroHeadline: House Panel Sets Sept. 15 Hearing on 'Totalitarian' Ortega-Murillo Regime as OAS Ministerial Date Splinters Between Sept. 17 and Sept. 28
heroSubtitle: The House Foreign Affairs Committee's Western Hemisphere Subcommittee confirmed a September 15 hearing on the Ortega-Murillo government after two prior postponements, landing as reporting on the long-delayed OAS foreign ministers' meeting on Nicaragua grew inconsistent — some coverage still pointing to a September 17 session while OAS Secretary General Albert Ramdin's own September 10 remarks named September 28, 'shortly after the UN General Assembly,' as the date under discussion with Washington. UN High Commissioner Volker Türk separately cited Nicaragua's closure of opposition parties in his September 7 global update opening the Human Rights Council's 63rd session.
